key_insight: NeuTNN-AV achieves competitive audio-visual classification with 4-bit weights, local learning, and far fewer synapses than leading spiking neural network baselines.
engineering_relevance: Its comparison-and-addition inference offers a hardware-efficient route to multimodal edge AI, although the abstract does not evaluate solid mechanics applications.
method: Use neurons with multiple active dendritic segments and temporal coding in which each input line spikes at most once.
Learn 4-bit integer weights through local reward-modulated spike-timing-dependent plasticity.
Support single-pass training and online adaptation to unseen actors.
evidence_signal: NeuTNN-AV achieves 78.6% on CREMA-D with 2.34M synapses and 98.82% on UrbanSound8K-AV with 1.38M synapses; the abstract reports 23–106× smaller weight memory and 100–1,000× lower measured synaptic energy than spiking baselines.
watch_item: Reported synaptic energy savings do not establish end-to-end system efficiency, including preprocessing, encoding, and hardware overhead.
paper_title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning
